eligibility.quote: This is a bug in `tf2_ros_py`. The `time_jump_callback` method needs a `self` argument.

failed_conditions.quote: The type annotation `def time_jump_callback(time_jump: TimeJump):` is incorrect. The first argument of a method is always bound to an instance of the class, and by convention this argument is usually called `self`. If I fix the argument name and the type annotation then the reason for the error becomes clear: `def time_jump_callback(self: "Buffer"):`. `Buffer.time_jump_callback()` takes 1 positional argument (a Buffer instance) but 2 were given (a Buffer instance and a `TimeJump` instance).

loudness.quote: TypeError: Buffer.time_jump_callback() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given

resolution.quote:
this fixes the problem all the way to rqt-tf-tree in jazzy! now i get 
[WARN] [1727982819.603705139] [tf2_buffer]: Detected jump back in time. Clearing tf buffer.
when without the fix rqt would crash, as expected.

notes: Independently verified: issue body shows the rqt reproduction and "[1]    295333 IOT instruction (core dumped)  rqt --ros-args -p use_sim_time:=True" after the TypeError; sloretz's diagnosis comment (fetched by id 2392115230) is verbatim as quoted. Commit 646342c6164e837d69460e3d28e7a025396544f6 ("Fix the time_jump_callback signature. (#711) (#712)", cherry-picked from efc78459) patches exactly one line: "-    def time_jump_callback(time_jump: TimeJump):" "/ "+    def time_jump_callback(self, time_jump: TimeJump):" — confirming the spec's resolved revision is the identical diff the reporter tested on jazzy. Eligibility: the failure is the arity of a callable crossing the rclpy library boundary (registration accepts it; invocation crashes), an interface failure whose resolving edit is inside the consumer — E2.2's carve-out applies; stop_step 6 is right. Class `other` is right: the consumer's declaration was always misformed (nothing renamed/retyped between revisions), and no listed class names a callable-signature mismatch. Loudness: silent_documented/run is right — the mismatched callback is accepted at registration and fails only at invocation as a run-time Python exception; the reporter's note that pyright would flag it but none ran supports silence. Resolution: observed is right — the reporter confirmed the working composition, rclpy is stated at 7.1.2 and unchanged, tf2_ros_py's resolved revision is the jazzy backport commit containing exactly the tested one-line change.
